best_for: Developers who juggle several branches or coding agents in one repository and want to commit to each without stashing and switching.

points.title: Several branches at once
points.text: GitButler keeps multiple branches active in one working folder, so you can assign changes to each without switching. It works on any existing Git repository.

points.title: Undo almost anything
points.text: Every operation is recorded and can be reverted. You can move, split, reorder and amend commits without an interactive rebase.

points.title: App, CLI and terminal UI
points.text: The desktop app, the `but` command line and a terminal interface share the same state, and coding agents can drive it through the CLI.

points.title: AI uses your choice of provider
points.text: Commit message and branch name generation uses GitButler's hosted OpenAI service by default, with no key needed. You can switch to your own OpenAI or Anthropic key, or local models through Ollama or LM Studio. Each project has to opt in.

points.title: Source-available, MIT after two years
points.text: The license is the Functional Source License 1.1. You may use it for anything except building a competing product, and each release becomes MIT two years after it ships. Flathub lists it as not a free license for that reason.

points.title: Windows trails macOS here
points.text: The Windows MSI is x64 and installs machine-wide. The Windows listing keeps 147 versions, but its latest was 0.22.3 while macOS was at 0.23.5. macOS and Linux list only the current release; the Flatpak is verified for x64 and Arm64.
